title: Russian state television shows Alabuga drone plant producing Geran-2 drones in Tatarstan
body:
In July 2025, Russia's Defense Ministry television channel Zvezda showed what it called the largest and most secret drone plant in the world, located at the Alabuga industrial park near Kazan in Tatarstan. The plant, built in 2023, has metal foundries, blacksmith shops and in-house assembly lines. Timur Shagivaliev, chief executive of the Alabuga Special Economic Zone, made claims about its output. Ukrainian drone strikes had previously targeted the facility, most recently reportedly on 15 June.

The plant produces the Geran-2, Russia's version of Iran's Shahed-136. The Geran-2 is 3.5 metres long, carries a 50 kg warhead, has a range of 1,800 km, flies at about 300 km/h and costs an estimated 35,000 to 49,000 dollars per unit. Parts were reportedly delivered from Iran via the Caspian Sea and the Kama River. The plant was reported to make 5,200 Shahed-type strike and decoy drones a month as of May, and Shagivaliev said output was nine times the original plan. Russia launched more than 5,300 Shahed drones in June, and on 9 July Ukraine faced its largest single-day attack, with 741 aerial weapons.

Russian state media showed teenagers assembling drones, and a recruitment programme targeted students as young as 15 from local technical colleges. The Kyiv Independent also reported that the zone recruited African women under false pretences through a work-study scheme, and that Interpol had opened a potential human trafficking investigation in April.
